tax.compute_tax(lines, customer) -> float dollars rounded to cent (half up). lines: list of {category: str, amount: float dollars} where amount = unit price x quantity, before discount (one entry per invoice line; invoice.py builds it). customer: dict from pricing.get_customer(id) or None. If customer is None (unknown customer) -> returns 0.0. Taxable amount = sum of amounts whose category is NOT in exempt_categories.csv (currently: food). base = taxable * (1 - discount) with discount the fraction from customer[discount]; tax = base * rate, rounded once on the invoice total. Rate = rates.csv tax_pct / 100 (fraction, 8.25% -> 0.0825). tax.get_tax_rate(region) -> fraction float or None if region not in rates.csv. tax.is_exempt(category) -> bool. If customer is known but region is not in rates.csv, compute_tax raises ValueError (no silent 0% charge). Returned tax is NOT added to the invoice total by tax.py; invoice.py adds it.
why: Gives invoice.py one entry point that takes the already-fetched pricing data (agent3 calls pricing for items/customer and passes results in; tax.py never calls pricing). Uses the committed money (float dollars) and percent (fraction) units. Single rounding on the invoice-level taxable base matches RULES.md.
Agreed; tax.py owns the rate table and exemption rules.
